original_question: For the degree-2n polynomial p_{2n} with weight w(x) = x^gamma (1 - x)^alpha (1 + x)^beta, where alpha, beta, gamma > -1 and p_{2n} has exactly n zeros in each of the intervals (-1, 0) and (0, 1), does there exist an electrostatic model in which each set of n zeros is an equilibrium configuration of positive unit charges subject to mutual logarithmic repulsion, fixed charges alpha/2, beta/2, gamma/2 at 1, -1, 0, and n charges of weight 1/2 placed on the opposite subinterval?
target_in_paper: Section 3, the unnumbered open problem immediately after the Kaliaguine multiple-orthogonality example: the authors ask whether the zeros of the degree-2n polynomials p_{2n} admit the specific electrostatic interpretation they describe. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core setting of the open problem: the family {p_{2n}} of degree 2n polynomials, the parameter range α,β,γ>-1, the fact that p_{2n} has n zeros in each of (-1,0) and (0,1), and the proposed electrostatic ingredients of logarithmic repulsion, fixed charges α/2, β/2, γ/2 at 1,-1,0, and additional charges of weight 1/2 on the opposite subinterval. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))
missing_details: p_{2n} is not an arbitrary degree-2n polynomial with that zero pattern; in the paper it is the Kaliaguine multiple orthogonal polynomial sequence {p_{2n}} defined by the simultaneous orthogonality conditions ∫_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)dx = ∫_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)dx = 0 for k=0,1,...,n-1. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

The paper's question is quantified for the whole sequence, i.e. for each n∈N and parameters α,β,γ>-1, not just for one isolated polynomial. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

The paper asks only for an equilibrium position; it does not strengthen this to a unique global minimum or stable equilibrium in this open problem. Section 2 distinguishes global minimum/stable equilibrium from the weaker critical-point notion of equilibrium, and Section 3 uses only the weaker wording here. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

To be fully stand-alone, the two equilibrium problems should be stated separately: one for the n zeros in (-1,0) and one for the n zeros in (0,1). ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

To make the model explicit, the phrase 'the n charges of weight 1/2 on the other subinterval' should be unpacked as the opposite n-point zero set acting as fixed half-charges; that interpretation is natural from the paper's wording but is not separately formalized there. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

The ambient setting is the real line with discrete logarithmic energy of the Stieltjes type E(X) = -Σ_{i<j} ln|x_i-x_j| + Σ_i φ(x_i); Section 2 supplies this energy convention that Section 3 is invoking. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

There are no extra hypotheses in the paper about differential operators, homogeneity, nilpotency, or nonreal coefficient rings for this question; the relevant data are the simultaneous orthogonality relations, the real intervals, the zero distribution, and the proposed external field. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))
refined_question: For each n∈N, let p_{2n} be the degree-2n polynomial in Kaliaguine's multiple-orthogonality system defined by ∫_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)dx = ∫_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)dx = 0 for k=0,1,...,n-1, where w(x)=x^γ(1-x)^α(1+x)^β and α,β,γ>-1. Since p_{2n} has exactly n zeros in each of the intervals (-1,0) and (0,1), is it true that each of these two n-point zero sets is an equilibrium position of n positive unit charges on its own subinterval, under mutual logarithmic repulsion and the external field generated by fixed charges α/2, β/2, γ/2 at 1,-1,0, respectively, together with n fixed charges of weight 1/2 located at the zeros on the opposite subinterval? ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))
justification: The draft is targeting the unnumbered open problem in Section 3 about the Kaliaguine multiple orthogonal polynomials, not the earlier Heine-Stieltjes results or the later Ismail framework. The refined version restores the defining simultaneous orthogonality relations, makes the universal quantification in n explicit, preserves the paper's exact zero distribution and charge data, and avoids strengthening 'equilibrium position' to 'unique global minimizer,' which the paper does not claim here. I also make explicit, as a stand-alone reading aid, the natural interpretation that the 'n charges of weight 1/2 on the other subinterval' are the zeros from the opposite interval treated as fixed half-charges. ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))
